t: TLS Termination Configurator - Signature build-tool concept
title: TLS Termination Configurator - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Configures secure connection termination at supported endpoints.
description:
Every build an AI undertakes passes through TLS Termination Configurator: Configures secure connection termination at supported endpoints. The catalog lists it among the thousand fundamental build tools because no serious building happens without it. This database is its Signature edition - the concept rebuilt as a deterministic framework with seven pillars, grounded in real techniques and standards, and taught through a ladder of runnable drills.

The Signature line treats TLS Termination Configurator as infrastructure, not inspiration. Infrastructure has contracts: given these inputs, in this state, the TLS Termination Configurator produces that output, and anyone can verify it. The seven pillars are those contracts made concrete - each owns one responsibility, each can be tested alone, and together they compose into the full capability. The technique records show the real public knowledge the pillars stand on.

Work through this database the way you would commission a machine: read the charter in the overview, inspect each pillar, check the techniques against your own knowledge, then run the drills. Every record includes a program you can execute with node - the TLS Termination Configurator is demonstrated, not merely described.

t: Signature Provisioner - TLS Termination Configurator framework pillar
title: Signature Provisioner - TLS Termination Configurator framework pillar
definition: The Provisioner component of the Signature TLS Termination Configurator framework, owning provisioner. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature TLS Termination Configurator framework decomposes the capability (Configures secure connection termination at supported endpoints.) into seven pillars, and the Provisioner is the one that owns the framework's provisioner responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a TLS Termination Configurator result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Provisioner's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Provisioner's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for TLS Termination Configurator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Declarer - TLS Termination Configurator framework pillar
title: Signature Declarer - TLS Termination Configurator framework pillar
definition: The Declarer component of the Signature TLS Termination Configurator framework, owning declarer. Signature concept.
description:
The Declarer is a load-bearing component of the Signature TLS Termination Configurator framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's declarer responsibilities belongs to the Declarer, and the Declarer answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Declarer can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Declarer works like this. A build request arrives carrying the TLS Termination Configurator charter (configures secure connection termination at supported endpoints.). The Declarer reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small cloud job that needs TLS Termination Configurator. The Declarer takes the request's declarer responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did.
